description: A pure CALCULATION node — Douglas–Peucker simplify a graph: collapse dense / wobbly polylines into a few straight segments. Graph in, graph out; draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: graph as JSON in, simplified graph as JSON out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

Use it to turn a hand-drawn or vectorised stroke (one vertex per pointer sample — hundreds of tiny edges) into a road-like network of a few straight runs. Runs Ramer–Douglas–Peucker on every polyline: interior vertices within Tolerance of the straightened line are dropped, endpoints and real corners are kept.

Tolerance is in METRES — bigger = fewer, straighter segments. A good starting point for freehand roads is ~0.3 m.

INPUT: wire Freehand Geometry / Graph Geometry val-graph into valin-graph. OUTPUT: val-graph — chain into Graph Reduce (Dissolve) to fuse junctions, or into a Network node to draw. Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
